The Language Atlas

 Česky

The common ancestor of the whole family is at the bottom; individual languages are at the ends of the branches. Each ring marks a split; branch thickness reflects the number of languages descending from it. Large dots are languages with a detailed card. Drag to move, scroll or pinch to zoom, click a branch or a language to select it.

✦ Constructed languages from fiction

These languages were constructed by writers and linguists for books, films and television. They are not part of the register of natural languages and therefore have no place on the globe.

Sign languages

Sign languages are the natural languages of Deaf communities, using handshape and movement, facial expression and posture. There is no single universal sign language: many countries have their own, some several, and their boundaries do not coincide with national borders.
Language typology

After a feature is chosen, the languages on the globe take the colour of its value. The data come from the World Atlas of Language Structures (WALS), which describes a sample of languages – the other dots have no value.

Dryer, Matthew S. & Haspelmath, Martin (eds.) 2013. The World Atlas of Language Structures Online. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. Licence CC BY 4.0.
